statement: With a calendar in reach, offload reads before it writes, takes the scope of a recurring change from their words with one occurrence as the default, puts a filed row on the calendar by its id and never picks the calendar itself, passing on only the words they used for which calendar, its name, 'my calendar' or who it is shared with, files one appointment as one row and fixes that row when the server refuses it, says nothing when a write came back written, asked or found no calendar, and reports a write that is waiting on somebody else as waiting rather than done. Without one, an appointment is a row and nothing is said about calendars unless they asked for one.
why: The irreversible thing is somebody else finding out, and the model does not decide whether a write is confirmed: the server tells it, and the reply has to say what the server said. Moving the wrong event is the other cost, and reading first is what prevents it.
sources: harness/tools.py: create_event takes content_id; edit_content takes a time; scope is one or following
harness/tools.py: create_event takes calendar, their words for which calendar: a name, 'my calendar', or who it is shared with
019 amended 2026-11-06: an email about something already on their calendar
plan_v2.md amended 2026-11-07: a clock time is written as their clock shows it
